doc.title: Jimmy Witherspoon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, FL, April 12, 1996

title: Touring Japan with Count Basie
summary: He toured Japan with Basie, wishing he could have afforded to stay; names band members and bassist Buddy Catlett.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: We just got through watching some old Basie movies. You could hear everything, even the bass, you could hear everything. You could hear the singing. Now didn’t you travel to Japan with Basie?
I’ve been doing some reading. What was that like?

Wonderful. Being with Basie man, was, I wish I could have afforded to stay in that band. He and I talked and financially, he couldn’t pay me what I wanted. But that was like being the Vice President of the United States. Benny Powell, what a great man. I was in the big, the best band.
Frank Wess, Frank Foster, you name ‘em. Marshall Royal, Ernie Royal.
Who was in the rhythm section at that time? Sonny Payne maybe?
Sonny Payne, Buddy Catlett. Buddy Catlett is in that new movie I just did, “Georgia.” That’s him playing bass.
All right. Can’t wait to see that. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
It must have felt pretty good to stand in front of that group. And what was the audience reaction like in Japan?
